title: Send Status Information to IRC Client on BNC Connect
instructions: When an IRC client connects to the BNC server, the BNC should send initial status information such as connection status, current nickname, joined channels, available networks, and any buffered messages. This improves the user experience so the client does not just sit silently after connecting.

1783339164.6129656.instruction: Modify the IrcConnection class in client/connection.py to replace the hardcoded AF_INET socket creation with socket.getaddrinfo(). This will allow the system to resolve both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. The getaddrinfo call should pass the host, port, and use AF_UNSPEC to get all available address families. Then iterate through the results and try to connect to each address until one succeeds.

1783339166.6028326.instruction: In the IrcConnection.connect() method, when creating the socket, check if the address family is AF_INET6. If so, create the socket with IPV6_V6ONLY set to 0 to allow dual-stack support on systems that support it. This ensures the socket can handle both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic if needed.

1783339168.66733.instruction: Modify the BncServerConfig class in config/settings.py to support IPv6 bind addresses. Update the bind_host default from "0.0.0.0" to support "::" (IPv6 any address) or "::ffff:0.0.0.0" (dual-stack). Also ensure the BNC server can accept connections on both IPv4 and IPv6 if configured.

1783339170.4753275.instruction: Modify the get_stats() method in IrcConnection class to include the address family (IPv4 or IPv6) of the current connection. This helps with debugging and verifying that IPv6 connections are working correctly.
